question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the researcher's claim?

options.A: City A had an electric-vehicle share of 4%, the lowest of the four cities compared.
options.B: City D had the fewest charging stations of the four cities yet the highest electric-vehicle share, at 22%.
options.C: City D, with the most charging stations at 18 per 10,000 people, had the highest electric-vehicle share at 22%.
options.D: City B and City C reported identical electric-vehicle shares despite having different numbers of charging stations.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text's implication?

options.A: Bleaching is triggered by a drop in water temperature rather than by a rise past a threshold.
options.B: Coral polyps that have expelled their algae can survive indefinitely, since the calcium carbonate they secrete supplies energy.
options.C: A reef's prior exposure to gradual warming can influence how severely it bleaches during a heat spike.
options.D: All coral reefs harbor algae strains that are equally tolerant of heat, whatever the waters around them have done.

question: Which finding, if true, would most strongly support the historian's claim about how the press spread the Reformation?

options.A: Printed Bibles were most abundant in the cities that had the highest adult literacy rates.
options.B: In the regions where Reformation ideas spread most rapidly, adult literacy rarely exceeded fifteen percent.
options.C: Catholic authorities also commissioned printed broadsides to circulate their own counterarguments.
options.D: Reformation tracts sold more copies than any earlier genre of printed book.

question: Which choice best captures the 'subtler revision' the passage proposes?

options.A: Monument-building may have been among the causes of agriculture rather than a result of it.
options.B: The site's builders had already domesticated wild cereals before they raised the enclosures.
options.C: The unusual density of the region's wild cereals made monument-building unnecessary for the site's builders.
options.D: Agriculture and monument-building arose at the same time but developed independently of each other.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the economist's claim?

options.A: Country Y had a higher average income than Country Z, 35 thousand USD, despite a lower literacy rate.
options.B: Country Z had the highest literacy rate, 97%, and also the highest average income, 33 thousand USD.
options.C: Country X had the highest literacy rate of the four but only the second-highest average income.
options.D: Country W had the lowest literacy rate of the four, 62%, and an average income of 8 thousand USD.

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Orbital shifts, rather than carbon dioxide, account for both the onset and the eventual magnitude of the last deglaciation.
options.B: Ice-core records demonstrate that changes in carbon dioxide concentration could not have influenced past global temperatures.
options.C: High-resolution dating of ice cores has become precise enough to distinguish events separated by only a few centuries.
options.D: Although carbon dioxide did not initiate the last deglaciation, it was essential to the full magnitude of the resulting global warming.

question: It can most reasonably be inferred that the theorist would regard a realist passage that strikes readers as especially "artless" as

options.A: proof that transparency in fiction is achievable without reliance on literary convention.
options.B: an especially skillful deployment of naturalized conventions rather than an absence of craft.
options.C: a failure of realism, since genuine realism should make its techniques visible to the reader.
options.D: evidence that free indirect discourse is incompatible with the realist illusion.

question: Which choice is best supported by the text?

options.A: Miss Everly resents customers who remark on how little has changed.
options.B: Miss Everly feels a pull toward change that she does not act on openly.
options.C: Miss Everly is indifferent to the shop's arrangement, having settled it long ago.
options.D: Miss Everly means to sell her father's shop once the ledgers are settled.

question: Which choice best describes what the researchers infer about verbose patent descriptions?

options.A: They indicated that inventions from regions with poor roads were more complex than those filed elsewhere.
options.B: Their thoroughness rose to offset inventors' limited ability to demonstrate devices in person.
options.C: They were written by inventors who distrusted their own physical prototypes.
options.D: They reflected the stricter legal standards that patent offices imposed on filings from regions with poor roads.

question: Which finding, if true, would most strengthen the reconsolidation account described in the text?

options.A: Memories left undisturbed for many years proved far more error-prone than memories rehearsed repeatedly, whose details stayed close to those of the original event.
options.B: Emotionally charged events were recalled far more often, and in more detail, than emotionally neutral ones.
options.C: Memories that people rehearsed every week were later reported with far greater confidence than memories recalled only once.
options.D: Memories recalled alongside misleading details were later reported with those details incorporated, while memories not recalled retained the original details.

question: It can most reasonably be inferred that paying for blood donations reduced participation because the payment

options.A: recast a meaningful act into a transaction that donors found unappealing.
options.B: signaled that the blood supply was in more urgent need than donors had assumed.
options.C: attracted less committed donors who crowded out the original altruistic ones.
options.D: was too small an amount to motivate people who would otherwise have donated for free.

question: Which choice is best supported by the evidence in the passage?

options.A: The region's population grew rapidly in the final period, outstripping the settlement's grain stores.
options.B: Residents packed the pits with pottery and ash to seal them against flooding.
options.C: A neighboring community attacked and destroyed the settlement at the end of its occupation.
options.D: The residents abandoned grain storage gradually as cereal farming in the region declined.

question: Which choice is most strongly supported by the text?

options.A: An authentic-instrument performance can reproduce a work's original sounds without reproducing how its original audiences perceived them.
options.B: Because listeners' perceptions have changed, Baroque music can no longer produce any effect on modern audiences.
options.C: The main obstacle to authentic performance is the difficulty of reconstructing period instruments and tunings from surviving treatises and specimens.
options.D: Using period instruments and tunings lets modern listeners hear Baroque works as their first audiences did.

question: Which choice best expresses what the historian implies about the tax ledgers?

options.A: Tax collectors deliberately overlooked the copper trade to favor certain merchants.
options.B: Perishable goods generated more total revenue for the city than durable metals did, because each shipment was assessed every time it changed hands.
options.C: The frequency of entries reflects how often goods were taxed rather than their overall economic importance.
options.D: The metal trade was economically insignificant compared with the trade in perishables.

question: The main purpose of the passage is to

options.A: determine which physical feature accounts for the old violins' superior tone.
options.B: establish that modern violins sound better than old Italian instruments.
options.C: explain why double-blind testing has become the standard method in acoustics research.
options.D: call into doubt whether the superiority that decades of research have tried to explain is real.

question: Which choice is best supported by the passage regarding why resurrection plants survive severe drying?

options.A: They store enough sugar to feed their cells through the long months in which they appear to be dead.
options.B: They revive within hours of rainfall because they take up and distribute water far more efficiently than other plants.
options.C: They use accumulated sugars to physically preserve cell structures when water is lost.
options.D: They avoid dehydration altogether by preventing water from leaving their cells during a severe drought.

question: The passage is primarily concerned with

options.B: arguing that ethnic diversity has no effect on any social outcome.
options.C: defending the original finding against its political critics.
options.D: reinterpreting an established correlation by identifying a confounding factor.

question: Which finding, if true, would most strengthen the revisionist claim that the return of the wolves was not sufficient to produce the vegetation recovery?

options.A: Elk populations fell sharply in the years immediately after wolves were reintroduced.
options.B: Willow stands failed to recover where water tables were low, despite a heavy and sustained wolf presence.
options.C: Beaver colonies increased across much of the park following the reintroduction of wolves.
options.D: Wolves hunted elk most successfully in the open bottoms of river valleys, where the browsing herds had few routes of escape.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the sociologist's claim?

options.A: The 45-54 and 55-64 groups volunteered at identical rates, showing no change between them.
options.B: The 35-44 group volunteered at 42%, the highest rate recorded for any of the four age groups.
options.C: As age increased from the 35-44 group to the 65-74 group, the volunteering rate fell from 42% to 24%.

question: Which finding, if true, would most strongly support the argument about the "rebound" effect?

options.A: After a region adopted far more efficient air conditioners, total electricity used for cooling rose as households that had previously gone without began cooling their homes.
options.B: A factory that installed more efficient motors reported a measurable drop in its monthly energy bills over the following year, with no change in the hours its production lines ran.
options.C: Efficient appliances often cost considerably more to buy than the less efficient models they replace, so a household needs several years of lower bills to recover the difference.
options.D: In markets where demand for a service was already saturated, greater efficiency cut total consumption by very nearly the full amount that the engineering improvement had predicted.

question: Which choice best captures what the daughter comes to suspect about her father's care for the garden?

options.A: He tends the garden as a substitute for confronting his grief rather than as genuine remembrance.
options.B: He maintains the garden to honor his wife's memory even more sincerely than the admiring visitors realize.
options.C: He has lost all interest in the garden and keeps it up only because visitors expect it of him.
options.D: He harbors a secret resentment toward his late wife and keeps her garden out of guilt for feeling it.

question: Which choice is best supported by the study described in the passage?

options.A: Individuals working alone are more accurate than groups in every case, since they spend longer with each car's repair history.
options.B: Groups reach more accurate judgments than individuals when given enough time to review the documents.
options.C: The accuracy of a group's judgment depended heavily on whether its first confident speaker was correct.
options.D: Participants who spent the longest with the repair histories were the ones who spoke first and most confidently in their groups.

question: Based on the passage, which statement about deep-sea bioluminescence is most strongly supported?

options.A: Anglerfish are among the few midwater predators that hunt by spotting silhouettes against the light from above.
options.B: The downward glow of ventral photophores draws prey more effectively than an anglerfish's dangling lure does.
options.C: Luring lights evolved earlier than the downward-directed glow of counterillumination and were gradually replaced by it in the ocean's midwaters.
options.D: For most deep-sea species, bioluminescence functions to reduce their visibility to predators below them rather than to attract prey.
